clue.text: The PM's old bag

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Victorian prime minister, four times in office; the 's reads as 'is'
second meaning: an old-fashioned hinged leather travelling case named after him

explanation.surface: A jibe at the Prime Minister's wife, calling her an old bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the 's as 'is': the prime minister is the bag. A GLADSTONE bag is a hinged leather travelling case named after William Gladstone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian premier lent his surname to a style of portmanteau, so one word names both statesman and luggage.

clue.text: Writer has info: Hague's last Tory leader

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the last letter of Hague's

parts.note: William Hague's name, the possessive aside

indicators.note: the leader of Tory is its first letter

parts.note: the word Tory, from which only the leader is kept

explanation.surface: An author has the inside story on William Hague as the final Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean Genet was a French novelist and playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Genet was a French author of novels and plays.

clue.text: Port makes one an idiot

parts.note: an means one, as in an apple
twerp is British slang for a silly person

explanation.surface: A fortified wine turns a person into a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' wants to be the drink; it is a harbour city. Antwerp is Belgium's great seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major seaport in Belgium.

clue.text: Urban know-how way above Conservative cardinal

indicators.note: in a down clue the way sits above the rest

parts.note: a street is a road or way
red, the colour of a cardinal's robes

explanation.surface: City savvy that ranks above a Conservative churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' wants to be a churchman; it is the colour, cardinal red.
explanation.definitionFit: Street cred is credibility among the fashionable young, the savvy of city streets.

clue.text: In advantageous position, being single and having a hard-on

parts.note: one means single
up, crudely, for being aroused

explanation.surface: A single man with an erection reckons he is ahead of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: To be one up is to hold an advantage over a rival.

clue.text: Former Blair house has no bearing on where our taxes go

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the house has no south, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: Chequers is the Prime Minister's country residence
S, south, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A grumble that a Prime Minister's former home has nothing to do with public money.
explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the British Prime Minister's official country house in Buckinghamshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the UK government's treasury department, which receives tax revenue.

clue.text: Blair's first to meet the president's totty

indicators.note: the first of the word Blair's is taken, its opening letter alone

parts.note: the word whose opening letter is used
Abe, Lincoln's first name, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: Blair is introduced to the American president's young women.
explanation.walkthrough: Abe Lincoln stands in for 'the president'. Totty is British slang for attractive young women.
explanation.definitionFit: Totty and babes are both slang terms for attractive young women, viewed as eye candy.

clue.text: Without flipping Mowlam, Blair and Brown initially go down badly

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the initials go around the other piece
initially picks out the first letter of each of the two names
flipping means turning over, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Mo Mowlam was a Labour cabinet minister

explanation.surface: Labour's leaders flop without Mo Mowlam's help.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Mowlam was Northern Ireland Secretary under Tony Blair, with Gordon Brown as chancellor. 'Flipping' reads like a mild British swear word in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To bomb is to flop, as a show that fails with its audience.

clue.text: Bloody-minded sort creating personal stink — left the girl holding one

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective answer: bolshie, describing such a person

parts.note: BO is body odour

indicators.note: the girl holds one inside her

parts.note: she stands for a girl
I is one as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An awkward man leaves behind a smell and a woman to deal with it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolshie, from Bolshevik, is British slang for deliberately uncooperative.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshie means obstinately rebellious, deliberately difficult, as such a person is.

clue.text: A respected leader, type of bloke who prefers the US

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an eminent, admired political figure

definitions.text: type of bloke who prefers the US
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read cryptically: a man for the States

explanation.surface: An admired politician turns out to be the kind who sides with America.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into the States plus man.
explanation.definitionFit: A statesman is an experienced, respected political leader.

clue.text: Rent out wobbly balls

definitions.note: British slang exclamation for nonsense, the answer's sense as a verdict

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady and out of shape, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A lewd image of a letting agent's unsteady testicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls!' as a retort means rubbish, so the definition is a judgment on a claim rather than anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'balls' to a claim is calling it nonsense, i.e. false.

clue.text: Accountant suffering a press invasion is a comfort for Brian

indicators.note: the accountant suffers what follows, being on the receiving end of it
an invasion pushes the other pieces inside the accountant's letters

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
taken as written
a mill is a machine that presses or crushes

explanation.surface: An accountant hounded by reporters becomes a source of solace for someone called Brian.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye nicknamed Prince Charles 'Brian'; his long-time companion was Camilla Parker Bowles.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the Prince's partner and consolation, so a source of comfort to the man the magazine called Brian.

clue.text: "Would-be fund-raiser puts ordinary folk second," Tory let slip

parts.note: the people's means belonging to ordinary folk

indicators.note: letting something slip makes it fall out of place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A Tory blurts out that a charity bid treats the public as an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Branson's bid to run the UK National Lottery was called THE PEOPLE'S LOTTERY; it failed, hence 'would-be'.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a proposed scheme to raise money for good causes that never won the licence.

clue.text: Ball-crushing female trainer?

indicators.note: the female crushes the ball by squeezing it inside her

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
O is ball-shaped

explanation.surface: A man-eating woman who trains people, crushing their testicles.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies a fearsome female coach; the definition is the sports footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a sports shoe, the everyday British word for a sneaker.

clue.text: Arse has wrinkle ~ that's the underlying reality

definitions.note: a clause defining a noun phrase: the bottom line is what it all comes down to

parts.note: bottom is a politer word for the backside
a line on the skin is a wrinkle

explanation.surface: A crude observation that a wrinkled backside is the hard truth.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom line is the fundamental fact, the essential point once everything else is set aside.

clue.text: Subject to tabloid photo

parts.note: taken as written
pic is the tabloid word for a photograph

explanation.surface: Someone is at the mercy of a tabloid photographer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject to' looks like a phrase meaning liable to; the definition is the noun Subject alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject of a discussion or piece of writing.

clue.text: Try to slice off balls

parts.note: to test is to try out

indicators.note: gone off, spoiled, so the letters of slice are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of this word are the raw material

explanation.surface: A grim instruction to attempt castration with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls is the slang word for the male reproductive glands.

clue.text: "A grand place for a stiff one," could be, note, usual Mo Mowlam opening

definitions.text: A grand place for a stiff one

indicators.note: these letters could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: E is a musical note
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the opening of Mowlam is its first letter

parts.note: the surname whose first letter is used

explanation.surface: Mo Mowlam, the Labour minister, launching a grand tomb, fronted by a quote about stiffs.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'stiff' is slang for a corpse. Mo Mowlam was Northern Ireland Secretary under Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: A mausoleum is a stately tomb, a grand building housing the dead.

clue.text: PM heady, that is irritated, by over-the-top press reports

indicators.note: something irritated is stirred up, so these letters are disturbed into new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A light-headed Prime Minister annoyed by sensational news coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Media hype is exaggerated, sensational coverage in the newspapers and broadcasting.

clue.text: Swinger's bit of underwear?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: something that hangs and so swings; the 's reads as 'is'
second meaning: a garter strap hanging from a belt to hold stockings up

explanation.surface: Lingerie belonging to a wife-swapping partygoer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the 's as 'is'. The swinger is not a partner-swapper but a thing that dangles, as a stocking strap does.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is a hanging garter strap, a piece of lingerie, and literally a thing that hangs down.

clue.text: Tone's a right naff politician

indicators.note: naff is British slang for tacky or rubbish, a hint that the letters are spoiled into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tony Blair, called Tone, is a thoroughly tacky politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for uncool or tacky.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elected lawmaker.

clue.text: City shows interest in spin

indicators.note: interest goes in the word for spin

parts.note: to turn is to spin
i is the abbreviation for interest in finance

explanation.surface: A city displays enthusiasm for political spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major industrial city in northern Italy, home of Fiat.

clue.text: Relentless competition produces a nation of arseholes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the exhausting scramble to get ahead at work
second meaning, read cryptically: a race, as in a people, made up of rats, i.e. nasty people

explanation.surface: Cutthroat rivalry turns a country into a land of jerks.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer: race as a people, rats as contemptible people.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the endless competitive struggle for success in working life.

clue.text: Boozers chosen by the Poles

parts.note: a candidate who is in has been elected
N and S, the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Heavy drinkers selected by voters in Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' wants to mean people from Poland; it is the two ends of the earth. A boozer is British slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Boozer is British slang for a pub, and an inn is a pub.

clue.text: I march past casually, displaying organ

indicators.note: done casually, without order, so these letters fall into a different arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Someone strolls by idly, flashing a body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests anatomy; it means a publication. Paris Match is a French weekly news magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a newspaper or magazine that serves as a mouthpiece, as this French weekly is.

clue.text: As one spared the supreme sacrifice, is Monica finally over Bill?

definitions.text: As one spared the supreme sacrifice
definitions.note: a description phrase standing for the person: the one who was spared

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of Monica

parts.note: the name whose final letter is used
AC, short for account, which is a bill

explanation.surface: Asks whether Monica Lewinsky is finally over Bill Clinton, as though she survived a sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Abraham was told to sacrifice his son Isaac, but was stopped at the last moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical son of Abraham was saved from being offered up on the altar.

clue.text: Centre reveals Hague's extremes are archaic

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: William Hague's name, the possessive aside
art is the old form, as in 'thou art'

explanation.surface: A political centre shows William Hague's extreme views are outdated.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hague was the Conservative leader at the time.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its centre or core.

clue.text: National BSE fiasco engulfs Right

indicators.note: the jumbled letters swallow the right
a fiasco is a mess, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of BSE, mad cow disease, are the raw material

explanation.surface: A country's mad cow disaster swallows up the political right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' as a noun means a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Serb is a national, a citizen, of Serbia.

clue.text: See 11
'One former politician joins an airline' — just an old Arab story?

parts.note: a means one
Lib, a Liberal, a member of the party that became the Liberal Democrats
a means an
BA is British Airways

explanation.surface: Mocks a claim that an ex-MP joining an airline board is just a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Party merged into the Liberal Democrats in 1988, hence 'former'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves is a tale from the Arabian Nights collection.

clue.text: Work hard to clean up Bush

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to labour, as in scrubbing away

explanation.walkthrough: Bush reads as the American president, but here it is shrubbery.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to toil, to scour clean, and as a noun means low stunted vegetation.

clue.text: Stools making men erect, embarrassed and cross inside

definitions.note: plural in form, while the answer is a mass noun; stools means faeces

indicators.note: the cross is put inside the muddled letters
embarrassed men are thrown into disarray, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material
x is a cross

explanation.surface: Bar stools cause men to become aroused, red-faced and annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stools' wants to be seats; it is the medical word for faeces.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine stools are bodily waste, which is what excrement means.
